notes.summary: Busy week. The Fed held rates on Oct 28, but two officials voted for another hike. On Oct 29, Q3 GDP grew a stronger-than-expected 3.4% while September PCE inflation rose to 3.6%, so the economy is growing but prices are still running hot. Big tech earnings split: Microsoft beat, but Alphabet had its worst day since 2004 (about −13%) on a profit miss and heavy AI spending, and ServiceNow fell about 25% on slowing growth. Amazon reports Oct 29 after the close and AMD on Nov 3. The backdrop is unchanged: a war-driven oil shock keeps inflation high and the Fed leaning toward hikes, which is hard on stocks priced for fast growth.
notes.fed: The Fed raised rates in September, then held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10–2 vote; the two dissenters wanted another hike. It gave no clear signal about December.
notes.fedNext: The next meeting is Dec 8–9. On Oct 28 the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% (Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a hike) and said it wants more information before acting again. Since then, Q3 GDP grew 3.4% and September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% (core 3.1%), both on Oct 29. Markets price about one more quarter-point hike in 2026. Chair Warsh also said the Fed will hold fewer meetings starting in 2027.
notes.oil: The US–Iran war has largely shut the Strait of Hormuz since late February. Brent crude settled near $117 a barrel on Oct 23, a six-month high, as traders bet the U.S. could resume strikes on Iran; U.S. crude (WTI) was about $101 on Oct 26.
